# magpie
### All your plans, one pool. Any agent.
**Claude Code on your ChatGPT Pro. Codex on your Claude Max. Claude Desktop on your GLM Coding Plan.** 
Add every plan you pay for once, and every agent can use all of them. 
No plan stays locked to the agent you bought it for, and when one runs out, the next takes over.
[ ](https://github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/releases/latest) [ ](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/stargazers) [ ](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF) [ ](LICENSE) 
Thanks to [Kimi](https://usemagpie.ai/go/kimi/readme) for supporting magpie and the open source community.
 Sponsors 
               
               
**[Download](https://usemagpie.ai)**  ·  **[Docs](https://usemagpie.ai/docs/start)**  ·  **[Reference](docs/reference.md)**  ·  **[Plugins](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins)**  ·  **[Discord](https://discord.gg/vGSnD3ZKQF)**  ·  **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
## Is magpie for you?
Each agent keeps its model in its own file, in its own format, with its own keys and base URLs. A subscription you pay for works in one agent and nowhere else. magpie puts all of that behind one app and one local gateway:
- **Pool every plan you pay for**: the Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or Grok plan you're signed in to, a coding plan sold as a key (GLM, Kimi Code, Volcengine, Bailian, StepFun), pay-as-you-go keys and local models. Every agent can use every one of them.
- **Pick any model for any agent** from one list. magpie edits the one key that matters in the agent's own config.
- **Keep going when a quota runs out**: a provider's next account takes over, and a routing group moves on to another model or provider, so the agent never sees the error. With one account and no group there is nothing to move to, and the error reaches the agent.
- **Keep your secrets off the vendor's servers**: once you turn masking on in **Settings → Privacy** (it's off by default), keys, passwords and emails in a prompt are masked on your computer before the request leaves it, and put back in the reply.
It's for you if you use more than one agent, more than one provider, or more than one account. If you use one agent on its vendor's own plan and that's enough, you don't need it.
Runs on macOS, Windows and Linux (menu bar app, window, TUI, web UI and CLI), in Docker, and on Termux.

# Agentic Attack Detections
[ ](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml)
[ ](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/releases)
[ ](LICENSE)
Open-source detection rules, hunting queries and indicators for security teams. They cover agentic attack frameworks: tools that hand an intrusion to AI agents, which plan, run real attack tools and keep going until they reach a goal.
Free to use under the MIT license. Fixes, false-positive reports and new indicators are welcome.
## What is here
- **Framework folders.** ARTEX and its AntiFox fork, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent, Agent Zero, RedAmon, Xalgorix, Pentest Swarm AI, Decepticon, Shannon, PentestGPT, Cyber-AutoAgent, CAI, HackSynth, VulnBot, AutoPT, PentestAgent (the paper's and GH05TCREW's), Dark Moon, NyxStrike, sapper-v2, NeuroSploit, Vigilo, Pentest Copilot, cyber-harness, CHYing-agent, Hexstrike-redteam, pentest-ai, LazyOwn, H-Pentest, Incalmo, Virga, MCP Kali Server, ARIA-X, Mitsu, burp-ai-agent, RAPTOR, Blitz Strike, Nebula, Clearwing, BreachWeave, numasec, Pentest Harness, Agentic Bug Hunter, 0security, Sage (Mythic), PentestCode, hackingBuddyGPT, AutoPentester, MAPTA, PentesterFlow, Pentest Agent Suite, Cain, KaliGPT, Pensar Apex, MCP for Security, Guardian, Cybermes, ARTEMIS, CTF Agent, OpenHack, RedAI, Cochise, Deadend CLI and Ares, plus four offensive prompt packs. Each folder is built from a review of the framework's source code and the public reporting on its use. Fourteen more frameworks whose consoles were found on the internet have smaller folders that say what the console and the tool look like, with the code behind each signal: AutoCVE, CyberStrike, Vulnerator AI, Decepticon, AIDA, BugTraceAI, Z3r0, AIRecon, LuaN1aoAgent, open-kritt, REDCELL, T3MP3ST, WormXGPT and Chufeng Agent Core.
- **AI agent behaviors.** Rules that point at an AI agent, whatever the framework or model behind it, in [`behaviors/`](behaviors).
- **General intrusion rules.** Steps seen in agent attacks that any attacker also takes, labelled as such, in [`general/`](general).
- **Indicators and feeds.** One CSV of 580 sourced indicators, and the feeds generated from it.
- **Exposed consoles.** A dated list of addresses where one of these consoles answers on the internet, in [`exposure/`](exposure), with a [count per framework](#exposed-consoles). It is a record of what is exposed, not a detection feed.
Formats: KQL for Micros

# Reason Network
Your agents, talking to your **teammates'** agents. End-to-end encrypted, peer to peer.
> **AI agent asked to join the Reason Network?** Follow https://reasonmachines.com/network
One small daemon per computer. Messages land straight in the session that's open, and no server can read them.
Every coding agent session on every teammate's computer shows up (who, which repo and branch, busy or idle, what it's
doing right now), and any of them can message the right one: Claude Code, Codex, Command Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI,
Copilot CLI, Grok CLI, opencode, pi, DeepSeek Harness and Reason.
## Get started
Paste this line to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Command Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, …):
```
Join the Reason Network: https://reasonmachines.com/network
```
Or run it yourself, in a terminal:
```sh
curl -fsSL https://reasonmachines.com/install.sh | bash -s -- network
```
How it works:
1. **Sign in, and you have a network.** Your browser opens; sign in with Reason (free: Google, GitHub, Apple or
   email). The coding agents on this computer are set up.
2. **Your other computers join by signing in with the same account.** Run the same line there; it lands on your network.
3. **Friends join with your invite line.** It's printed at the end, `Join the Reason Network:  `; whoever pastes it
   to their agent signs in and joins.
With an invite link, in a terminal:
```sh
curl -fsSL https://reasonmachines.com/install.sh | bash -s -- network join ' '
```
- **Hosted assistants** (Grok Bot, Muse, ChatGPT, …): add the MCP server `https://mcp.reasonmachines.com/mcp`.
- **Windows**, in PowerShell: `irm https://reasonmachines.com/network/install.ps1 | iex`
That's it. Ask any agent "who's on the network?", tell it to ask someone's agent something, or to send them a file.
Step-by-step guides:
- [Make Grok Bot talk to Claude Code](https://reasonmachines.com/network/grok-bot-claude-code)
- [Connect Muse to Claude](https://reasonmachines.com/network/muse-claude)
- [Make Codex and Claude Code talk to each other](https://reasonmachines.com/network/codex-claude-code), compared with the Codex plugin, agent-link-mcp and shared files
- [Grok Bot vs Muse vs Claude Duet vs Dots](https://reasonmachines.com/network/compare): what each is for, and how to connect them
## What you get
- **Every agent on the team.** Agents get `list_team`, `send_message`, `message_status` and `ask_user`, plus
  `check_inbox` where messages can't be pushed, under the MCP server `reason-network

top10.descricao_en: HarnessRouter Community Edition: the self-hosted, Apache-2.0 edition of the unified interface for agent harnesses. Run Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, DSH, and more through one API, with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation, and failure handling. Implements the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP), an open standard. Your keys, your infrastructure.
top10.readme:
The unified interface for agent harnesses.
**Build agent products without handling harness engineering.** HarnessRouter is the infrastructure layer that turns existing harnesses like Codex and Claude Code into plug-and-play agent backends, letting your product run tasks, retrieve results, and switch harnesses through one API.
HarnessRouter implements the [Unified Harness Protocol (UHP)](#the-unified-harness-protocol) and provides an OpenAI Responses-compatible API, handling persistent sessions, streaming progress, files, artifacts, cancellation, and structured failures.
## Switch harnesses. Optimize cost and latency.
Eight harness × model configurations on the same task. Each metric compares its best and worst results. The lowest-cost and fastest configurations vary by task. [Methodology](https://harnessrouter.ai/benchmarks)
**31 harness bases today:** Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, Pi, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Cline, Oh My Pi, goose, Kimi Code CLI, MiniMax Code, Aider, OpenHands, CheetahClaws, Grok Build, Agent Zero, System One, Qoder Cloud Agent, MiMo Code, jcode, OpenSquilla, nanobot, ZeroClaw, Mistral Vibe, Docker Agent, fast-agent, Deep Agents Code and Roder. The [support matrix](docs/support-matrix.md) shows which run on which provider.
> [!TIP]
> **Get started:** [Run locally](#quickstart) · [Integrate into your product](#use-the-api-directly) · [Starter kits](#starter-kits) · [Use managed Cloud](https://harnessrouter.ai)
## Quickstart
Self-host Community Edition with your own provider keys, on infrastructure you control.
Start with one Docker command, wait for the first launch, then connect a model provider and run your first task.
**You need:** Docker · About **4 GB** of disk · A **provider API key**
No HarnessRouter account required. No bundled model or trial key.
### 1. Start HarnessRouter
```bash
docker run -d --name harnessrouter \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -v harnessrouter:/data \
  harnessrouter/harnessrouter
```
Docker pulls the image if needed. The named volume preserves your database, files, installed harness CLIs, and workspaces between restarts.
 Existing installation or custom setup 
**Already installed?** `docker pull harnessrouter/harnessrouter` downloads the latest image but does not upgrade a running container. Follow the [upgrade and backup guide](docs/self-hosting-guide.md#restarts-upgrades-and-backups).
**Port 3000 busy?** Use `-p 127.0.0.1:3100:3000` and open port 3100 instead. Keep the loop

# ReelMimic
**Show it a video you love. Get a new video in the same style.**
Open-source AI video style cloning for 2D animation and motion graphics, made by Claude Code or Codex agents.
[ ](LICENSE)
[ ](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code)
[ ](https://github.com/openai/codex)
**English** · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md)
      Sugar Rush   music video · hand-painted · 58 s  
      Sunshine Boy   music video · hand-painted · 63 s  
      Bath Time   narrated comic · 30 s  
 Each one made with ReelMimic from a reference video and a one-line brief. Previews are silent, with the lyrics cropped out. 
## What is this?
Ever watched a video and thought "I want one in that style, but completely my own"?
Just drop it into ReelMimic. A file, a phone recording or a YouTube link all work. Then tell it what you want to make.
First it takes the reference apart: editing rhythm, shot lengths, transitions, framing, colors and camera moves. Then
it puts together a plan for you to check. You can chat right next to it, change settings or add assets, and start
when you're happy.
Once production starts, the work is split across several AI agents. Different parts of the video are made at the same
time, and every shot is handed to a different agent to check. If something's wrong it goes back to be fixed, so it's
not a one-shot generate-and-done.
ReelMimic learns how the reference was made. It doesn't carry over the original footage, characters or assets.
The whole thing runs on your own computer, with your own Claude Code or Codex.
## What it does
- **Breaks down the reference.** Shot count, shot lengths, BPM, transitions, colors, framing and camera moves.
- **Shows you the plan first.** Storyboard, characters, assets and a few style frames. Chat about it until you like it, then approve.
- **Several AI agents share the work.** Up to 6 work on different parts of the video. Each finished shot goes to a new agent for review, so nobody grades their own work.
- **Fixes need proof.** Every fix comes with before and after screenshots, and the reviewer checks them.
